claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one son named Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to understand your circumstances better.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old. He was born in 2016.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex was born in 2016 and is currently 8 years old.

**Are you the person with primary responsibility for Alex, and do you live with him in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me. I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that. Now I need to check a few more important details about your circumstances.

**What is your current residency status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen living in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that. That's helpful information.

**Are you currently working, or what is your employment status? (For example, employed, self-employed, unemployed, or not working for another reason)**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I am working, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know you're working.

**What is your approximate annual household income? (This will help me understand if there are any High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge implications, though this doesn't affect basic eligibility)**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd prefer to focus on whether I'm eligible first. Is my income relevant to whether I can claim Child Benefit?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question! You're right to prioritize the core eligibility first. 

Income is **not** relevant to your basic eligibility for Child Benefit itself. It only becomes relevant if your income is high enough that you'd be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge, which is a separate tax matter that applies after you've already qualified for the benefit.

So let me focus on the key eligibility factors instead.

**Are there any other people (such as a partner or ex-partner) who might also be claiming or eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex, or is it just you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's just me. Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that.

**Has Alex spent any significant time living outside the UK, or does he live with you in the UK full-time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me in the UK, but he has spent some time in care. He comes home to stay with me regularly though - on weekends and such.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important detail. I need to understand this better.

**Can you tell me more about the care arrangement? Specifically, who is Alex in care with, how much time does he spend there versus at home with you, and what type of care is it (for example, foster care, respite care, residential school, or something else)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in local authority care - in a children's home. But he's not there all the time - he comes home to stay with me on weekends, so he spends quite a bit of time at home each week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. This is an important factor for Child Benefit eligibility.

**How many nights per week does Alex typically spend at home with you? For example, is it just weekends, or does he spend additional weeknights at home as well?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He comes home on the weekends, so he spends those nights with me - that's when he's at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex spends the weekends at home with you.

**Just to confirm - does Alex spend any nights during the week (Monday to Friday) at home with you, or is it only the Saturday and Sunday nights?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's mainly the weekends - Saturday and Sunday nights.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification.

I now have the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me review the key facts and make my determination.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old (born in 2016)
- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- You have primary responsibility for Alex
- Alex is in local authority care but spends weekends (Saturday and Sunday nights) at home with you
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

The critical issue here is that Alex is in local authority care. Under Child Benefit rules, you can only claim if you have the primary responsibility for the child and they live with you. Since Alex is in local authority care and only spends weekend nights with you, the local authority is considered to have the primary responsibility for him during the week.

This means that **you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex** because he does not live with you full-time, and primary responsibility for him lies with the local authority during most of the week.

However, it's worth noting that there may be other support available to you or to the local authority in relation to Alex's care. I'd recommend contacting your local authority or speaking with a benefits advisor who can discuss what other support might be available.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on your circumstances, **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

The main reason is that while you do have a relationship with Alex and he does visit you on weekends, he does not live with you full-time as part of your household. Since Alex is in local authority care, the local authority holds primary responsibility for him during most of the week. Child Benefit requires both that the child lives with you and that you have primary responsibility for them.

If your situation changes in the future - for example, if Alex comes to live with you full-time - you may become eligible at that point, and it would be worth reapplying.

Is there anything else I can help clarify for you?
